The most important thing about the New Deal program, which Keynesian supporters love so much, is that when it was implemented the federal government actually had money.

Like, a lot of money. Tons of money.

After the Civil War there were lots of barriers in place to prevent the federal government from interfering in state level politics in order to keep the peace, so to speak. The country had lots of money, but no way to get the money into the economy. The New Deal blew that all away, using federal money to support the states. FDR was able to implement the New Deal without having to bankrupt the nation.

Now fast forward to Obama in 2009, and we see that the situations are completely different even though so many on the left see the situations as comparable. Obama's plan was to spend money the government didn't have, and then recover that money by taxing the ones with the most capacity to create jobs. It just doesn't work, and anyone who's taken a college level economics class knows that there was no way the "stimulus" package could have worked.
